title: Adversarial Benchmarks and BenchDoor Attacks: Exploiting Benchmark Incentives for Backdoor Attacks
abstract: arXiv:2610.27533v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Machine learning benchmarks act as guideposts for model development and spur the creation of training datasets intended to improve benchmark scores. We introduce BenchDoor, a family of data poisoning attacks that exploits this incentive. Beyond preserving benign performance, BenchDoor requires benchmark gains that encourage adoption of data that also implants a backdoor. The adversary either manipulates a benchmark's training or test data, creating an adversarial benchmark, or supplies an independent training dataset while leaving the benchmark unchanged. We formalize five attack scenarios, including training on rewritten test examples and applying similarity-based decontamination. Across multiple-choice Q&A, text classification, and open-ended Q&A with Qwen and Gemma models, BenchDoor achieves positive benchmark gains for all 30 evaluated configurations, with held-out attack success rates of 82.33% to 100.00% at poisoning rates of 2%

translated_title: 对抗性基准与BenchDoor攻击：利用基准测试激励机制实施后门攻击
translated_abstract: 机器学习基准测试是模型发展的指引标杆，并推动了旨在提升基准分数的训练数据集的创建。我们提出了BenchDoor，这是一类利用该激励机制的数据投毒攻击。BenchDoor不仅要保持良性性能，还要求获得能促使相关数据被采纳的基准分数提升，而这些数据同时会植入后门。攻击者要么操纵基准测试的训练数据或测试数据，从而创建一个对抗性基准，要么在保持基准测试不变的情况下提供独立的训练数据集。我们形式化了五种攻击场景，包括在改写的测试样例上进行训练以及应用基于相似度的数据去污染措施。在多项选择问答、文本分类和开放式问答任务上，使用Qwen和Gemma模型，BenchDoor在全部30个评估配置中均实现了正向的基准提升，在2%的投毒率下，留出集攻击成功率达到82.33%至100.00%。
tldr: BenchDoor利用模型开发者追求基准分数提升的激励机制，将后门植入数据伪装成能带来基准增益的训练数据，在全部30个评估配置中均实现正向基准提升，并在2%投毒率下达到82.33%至100%的攻击成功率。
en_tdlr: BenchDoor exploits the incentive to improve benchmark scores by disguising backdoor-implanting data as benchmark-enhancing training data, achieving positive benchmark gains across all 30 evaluated configurations with attack success rates of 82.33%–100% at a 2% poisoning rate.
